annotations.title: Money value: inflation math from the official CPI

description: Exact inflation math for any country: what an amount from one year is worth in another, the total price change, the average yearly rate and the latest inflation rate. The US uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI-U (monthly, back to 1913); other countries use their national consumer price index as published by the World Bank (yearly). Use instead of estimating for questions like 'what is $100 from 1990 worth today?', 'what were 1,000 euros in 2000 worth in Germany now?' or 'what's inflation in India?'. Not for today's interest rates (use check_rates) or pay for a job (use check_wage).

amount.description: Amount in the country's currency (dollars for the US)

country.description: Country name or two-letter code; defaults to the United States. Amounts are in that country's currency.

from.description: Year (1990), or for the US a month (1990-06), the amount is from

to.description: Year or month to convert to; defaults to the latest figure
